question: The Critical Raw Materials Act, which entered into force on 23 May 2024, classes the Nussir copper mine as a strategic project1. It is partly financed by the EU. Although the RESourceEU Action Plan was published on 3 December 20252, a year and a half after the Critical Raw Materials Act entered into force, to date there have been no details nor any transparency concerning the financing of the projects.

This situation raises concerns as to the EU’s choices and guidelines when it comes to access to information on various projects and the selection of so-called strategic projects, in particular with regard to their environmental impact, such as that of the Nussir copper mine. 1.
How much EU funding is estimated to be spent annually on supporting each of the projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act, including those outside EU territory?
Does the Commission intend to seek sustainable and less restrictive solutions for replacing copper, a pollutant that is toxic for the environment and local populations?
